claim_en: THE ACCENTS PARSE THE NUMBER AND THE TOTAL PROVES THE PARSE. 'One pan, ten of gold' (7:14): the consonants 'one ten' spell ELEVEN (as at 2 Kgs 9:29); the ACCENTS cut them — the 'one' carries a tevir (a disjunctive) at all twelve pan-verses (7:14 to 7:80), while every 'eleven' written one-and-ten in the Tanakh (Gen 32:23, Deut 1:2, Josh 15:51, 2 Kgs 9:29) joins its 'one' to its 'ten' by a conjunctive or the joining stroke (computed on the DB's own marks); and THE TOTAL DECIDES: 7:86's 'all the gold of the pans, a hundred and twenty' = 12 × 10, not 12 × 11 — the very total the Sifrei uses to decide the pan was gold weighed in silver (row 49:1, 55:1) decides one-versus-eleven for the parser; 7:13's 'one' before 'a hundred and thirty' carries a revia, another disjunctive; the engine reads 11 and 131 — the compile's items; ONKELOS 'one pan, a weight of ten selas, it of gold' — the accents' parse and the Sifrei's answer in one rendering; the shekel written as the SELA at every weight (the conversion layer, one to one — Bekhorot 50a); the dish and the pan are 4:7's vessels.
middah: ink (the accents measured on the DB's own marks against every one-and-ten in the Tanakh; the total's arithmetic computed; the translation's parse cut from the shelf)
